title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
description:
You are given a list of `tokens` that encodes an arithmetic expression in **postfix (Reverse Polish) notation**. Each token is either an integer or one of the operators `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`.

Evaluate the expression and return the result. Division between two integers **truncates toward zero** (so `-7 / 2` is `-3`). The expression is guaranteed to be valid and no division by zero occurs; all intermediate values fit in a 32-bit signed integer.
constraints: Each token is an operator or an integer in [-200, 200]
hints: In postfix notation an operator applies to the two values that came just before it. What holds those two values?
Push numbers. On an operator, pop the right operand first, then the left, compute, and push the result.
Python's // floors toward negative infinity; use int(a / b) to truncate toward zero as the problem requires.
approach:
**Key insight: postfix notation needs no precedence rules.** By the time you read an operator, its two operands are the two most recently produced values, so a stack evaluates the expression in a single pass.

**Algorithm.** For each token: if it is a number, push it. If it is an operator, pop `b` then `a` (order matters for `-` and `/`), compute `a op b`, push the result. The single remaining value is the answer.

**Why it works.** A valid RPN expression is a post-order traversal of its expression tree; the stack holds the evaluated subtrees whose parent has not been seen yet.

**Common mistakes.** Popping operands in the wrong order (`b - a` instead of `a - b`). Using `//` for division, which floors: `-7 // 2` is `-4`, but the problem wants `-3`. Treating `"-11"` as an operator because it starts with `-`; test membership in the operator set, not just the first character.

**Interview follow-ups.** (1) Convert an infix expression to postfix (shunting-yard) and evaluate it. (2) Add unary minus or exponentiation. (3) Report an error on malformed input instead of assuming validity.
